I've been reading fantasy short stories and tales that have come before the era of Robert Jordan, Martin and Sanderson, even Farland or Brooks. Even Tolkien in some instances.

I have in most cases enjoyed these stories much much more than modern books. I have more of an imaginative reaction from reading the short story Bethmoora of the Dreamer's Tales books than lets say Mistborn (And I very much enjoyed that book).

I've read many of the Conan stories and I personally recommend A Witch Shall be Born (even though Conan fans apparently rate this as a mediocre addition to the stories).

You can see the impressions that these older stories have had on the modern fantasy genre, in the case of Martin I am convinced that he scoured "forgotten" fantasy works for "inspiration". While reading and being exposed to The Night Land I saw an instant connection with Martin's Shadow Lands and the area of Asshai where people with odd powers reside.

The authors of older fantasy works also would have had a proper education in creative writing, the classics and even myth and folklore instead of simply being exposed to other fantasy readers or other aspects of popular culture (on which I feel modern fantasy authors are too reliant).

Modern readers by not exposing themselves to these older texts, are really missing out and I encourage everyone to go out and look for pre-Tolkien fantasy as they might be surprised how much they are missing out on. I can also see in a generation or so that future fantasy writers might partake in a "retro" style of writing fantasy that might draw from these older styles.

Here here. While the style of prose can be difficult for a modern reader to wrap their head around, reading older works from another time, with different speech patterns, different values, different contemporary issues and folklore can be really interesting.
